ai.description: *Hylarana bahuvistara* is a medium-sized frog (35–55 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct white or yellow dorsolateral folds. It features a dark mask and mottled, pale-spotted hind limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana bahuvistara* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous white or cream-colored glandular fold along the upper lip that extends to the shoulder.
ai.habitat: *Hylarana bahuvistara* inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, often found near streams within the Western Ghats at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Wide-spread Fungoid Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for insects among the leaf litter and vegetation of forest floors.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana bahuvistara* breeds during the monsoon season, laying large clutches of eggs in stagnant water bodies, which develop into aquatic tadpoles.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hylarana bahuvistara* is found in the Western Ghats of India, spanning the states of Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Hylarana bahuvistara* consists of a series of short, pulsed notes with a low-frequency pitch, typically heard near forest streams and pools.
